articleTitle: Advances in modem technology since V.32/V.32bis
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: There have been significant improvements in modem technology since the development of CCITT Recommendation V.32. These improvements have been not so much in the basic performance/complexity characteristics of TCM as in reduced constellation expansion, robustness to nonGaussian impairments, suboptimal decoding methods, shaping gain, and combined equalization and coding. In addition, the PSTN has improved quite noticeably, and DSP computational power has dramatically increased. In combination, these factors will make possible V.fast modems that can transmit reliably at data rates up to twice as fast as V.32bis modems over the PSTN.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new structure for the equalisation of nonlinear channels
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: A structure capable of equalising communication channels consisting of a memoryless nonlinearity embedded between two linear subsystems is presented. The equaliser is initialised using a system identification procedure. Once initialised it is updated using a simple LMS-type algorithm. Some practical details of its operation are discussed and simulation results are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Flexible precoding for V.fast (modem)
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: In order to gain the most advantage from the high symbol rates, V.fast needs to be equipped with a powerful equalization technique that can effectively mitigate the amplitude distortion near the upper band-edge which can be as high as 3700 Hz. The author describes flexible precoding, a transmitter equalization technique, which is being considered for V.fast. Results indicate that flexible precoding combined with spectral pre-emphasis can provide excellent equalization in V.fast for all common channel impairments, including uncancelled echoes and signal-dependent impairments.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Pulse noise tolerance of trellis-coded modulations
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: The Gaussian noise performance of trellis-coded modulations is well known. The authors, however, analyze the tolerance of these systems to additive pulse noise, represented by baseband pulses of finite length and arbitrary shape. Pulse noise performance of trellis-coded modulation schemes with two-, four- or 8-dimensional constellations is examined. The compared schemes are among those being considered for a new high speed dial modem CCITT recommendation. A generalized pulse noise threshold formula for any convolutional codes is derived. They conclude that different trellis-coded modulation schemes can be very close in additive Gaussian white noise (AWGN) tolerance but differ dramatically in pulse noise immunity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nonlinear encoding by surface projection
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: High speed quadrature amplitude modulated modems use dense signal constellations to transmit multiple bits of information in each symbol interval. Modem tests reveal a significant increase in distortion near the perimeter of the signal constellation caused by signal-dependent impairments. A nonlinear encoding technique reduces perimeter distortion. The encoder projects the signal constellation points on a nonlinear surface prior to modulation. This surface may, for example, increase the margin or distance between perimeter signal points. The receiver projects the demodulated signal points on a reciprocal surface prior to decoding, restoring the signal points to their original uniform spacing, and compressing distortion on the perimeter points. The author, along with illustrations of the surface projected signal constellations, presents the nonlinear encoding technique. A data rate of 28800 bit/s is achieved using this technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Counteracting the quantisation noise from PCM codecs
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: Since a large majority of telecommunication connections now involve digital PCM, the quantisation noise from PCM codecs is of concern to those transmitting data. The authors present the effect on performance of passing a modem signal through PCM systems. They also assess the effectiveness of some simple coding schemes in counteracting the quantisation noise produced by PCM codecs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Passband echo cancellation techniques for high-speed modem applications
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: The author describes passband algorithms for the cancellation of data echoes in high-speed modems. The conventional, all-real single-filter canceler is discussed, along with the hybrid passband/baseband Weinstein canceler. In addition, a new passband echo canceler which exceeds the performance of some other fully-passband echo cancelers while limiting resource requirements is introduced. This canceler employs the concept of adding out-of-band noise to the adaptive filter input signal; this increases the number of degrees of freedom available to the echo canceler during convergence, thus increasing the level of echo cancellation achieved. The performance of each type of passband echo canceler is examined, and their relative performance is demonstrated. Some potential advantages and unique applications of the new noise-enhanced echo cancellation technique are identified.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Start-up requirements for V.fast modems
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: Start-up requirements for a new PSTN V.fast modem are reviewed. A new calling and answering procedure is proposed which meets the requirements of V.fast, and has other benefits. Start-up into half-duplex facsimile mode and into duplex transmission over international connections are both considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PSTN survey for V.fast studies
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: Much of the effort in the V.fast Rapporteur Group in CCITT Study Group XVII has been devoted to the definition of a test suite suitable for evaluating proposed modem technologies, which is representative of the public switched telephone network of today and the future. During the week of December 9-14, 1991, Motorola Codex implemented a test plan to capture a snapshot of today's switched network within Europe, and between Europe and North America. It is recognized that this is far from representing a scientific sample, however the results are indicative of what one should expect to find within the regions tested. The findings from this survey are summarised.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Normes Europeennes De Telecommunication (NETS) 20-25 and their impact on modem manufacturers and users
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: The modem market in Europe keeps growing. The average user, however, has no means to ascertain whether a model that he intends to buy has a satisfactory performance and would hence fulfil his needs. Standards have been developed in Europe which will allow modem manufacturers to achieve a certification of quality for their products, and which will give to the user confidence that the product has been tested and has been shown to have a reasonable performance. It is the aim of the author to clarify the situation and to make modem manufacturers and users more aware of the existence of these European standards, and of the bearing they may have on modem design, marketing and purchase.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adapting to the ISDN-which rate adaption scheme should I use?
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: The CCITT has standardised two rate adaption protocols for use over the ISDN. V.110 uses a fixed pattern of bits (frame) into which the user's data bits are fitted. Both synchronous and asynchronous data are supported, together with some end-to-end control signals. V.110 provides neither error detection nor correction facilities and operates only over a B channel using the circuit mode bearer service. V.120 encapsulates the user's data stream in HDLC frames. Three types of data are supported: asynchronous, HDLC framed synchronous and bit transparent synchronous. Error detection is provided for all types and for the asynchronous and HDLC classes, error correction is available as an option. V.120 can operate over a B channel using the circuit mode or frame relay bearer services or the D channel using frame relay only. Now that V.120 is a stable Recommendation it will start to be provided on TAs sold in Europe. Such TAs will almost certainly be multi-protocol, supporting V.110 as well. They will therefore continue to interwork with older V.110-only equipment whilst also solving the transatlantic compatibility problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Data communications in the ISDN era
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: The author addresses some of the key issues for successful data communications in the ISDN era and focuses on two prime areas, i.e. the understanding and use of ISDN services together with the selection of appropriate terminal apparatus. He highlights and describes some of the main difficulties and discusses scenarios for applications. He points out that these are early days for public ISDN data communications to International standards. The scene is now set for the innovative and flexible provisioning and use of these services. ISDN services together with emerging products and applications, addressing increasingly wider markets, will create benefits and advantages for business users.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Standardization opportunities with V.fast FAX/modem technology and ISDN terminal adaptors
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: It is expected that the ISDN and the PSTN will coexist for some time. The need for terminal adaptors to interface existing terminal equipment to the ISDN, and the need for functions in a terminal adaptor to facilitate interworking with the PSTN puts an important focus on the evolution of terminal adaptor equipment. The authors discuss the following topics: common terminal adaptor and modem services; new opportunities for standardisation in PSTN modems; new opportunities for standardisation in PSTN FAX machines; and ISDN/PSTN interworking.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Programming communication interfaces (PCIs)-T.611: a new CCITT standard API for Facsimile applications
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: In April 1992, the CCITT approved a new Recommendation, 'T.611-Programmable Communication Interface (PCI) Appli/Com for facsimile group 3, facsimile group 4, teletex and telex services'. The author discusses the main principles of the T.611 standard. He then discusses how this standard compares with other competitors and describes the kind of products that can derive from the T.611 standard.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Applications programming interfaces for communications (programmable communications interfaces)
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: The author focuses on the specific subset of (APIs) that provide interfaces between software applications and remote communications services. He describes the work occurring in CCITT, termed programming communications interfaces, to formalize application to wide area networking interfaces.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Remote file server over ISDN
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: The advent of ISDN as a digital telecommunication service brings many opportunities for new applications. Joining local networks over ISDN is one of the possible applications. To extend this concept, ISDN can be used to connect mobile platforms. This arrangement enables sites to be set up and made available for access over a wide geographical area. Such systems are referred to as remote file servers. Several protocol options can be built into these servers to allow communication at various levels. For example, FTP. The improvement from the basic file transfer between pre-arranged sites to global information acquisition is an advance towards the future of public data networks. The authors propose a design for an ISDN file server, discusses its protocol possibilities and estimate its efficiency adapted to different situations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Agile data rates via arithmetic base conversion
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: An arithmetic base converter provides highly flexible modem operation. The arithmetic base conversion is unconstrained by bit rate and symbol rate combinations. It converts a desired fractional number of bits per symbol to the appropriate arithmetic base. Fractional bit rate modulation allows high speed modems to operate in any bandwidth and at any data rate to optimize the channel bandwidth and signal-to-noise ratio. The symbol rate matches the optimum bandwidth of the channel. The number of points in the constellation subset is equal to the arithmetic base. The signal constellation is power indexed such that constellation power and size increase monotonically with data rate. This arrangement allows one constellation table to accommodate variable data rates with optimum packing for minimum power in all cases and a circular constellation shape to minimize peak factor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Combined Huffman and trellis decoders for data transmission
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: The principles of a new scheme for combining the source and channel coding applicable to digital communication systems is described. At the transmitter the concatenation of a source encoder with a channel encoder is considered. At the receiver, source and channel decoding are combined into a single decoding unit. This unit controls the transmission errors caused by the channel noise that error free data can be transferred to the user. The combining technique employing variable-length Huffman codes for source coding and variable rate convolutional codes for channel coding is described, together with its performance over an additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel. It is shown that combining source and channel coding is particularly applicable to digital communication systems where the effect of noise is severe, and thus reduces the overall complexity of the system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CCITT V.56 modem testing principles
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: The authors look at the history of CCITT Recommendation V.56. It's main principles are explained. Recent discussions and reports on the recommendation are covered, and the need for it to be modified is explained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: VLSI modem development and the race towards V.fast
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: The CCITT's pending V.fast recommendation for modem communication at data rates as high as 28.8 kb/s will advance the state of the art nearly to the theoretical capacity of the public switched telephone network (PSTN). Because it will set the standard for modem communication indefinitely, V.fast ultimately will have to encompass the advanced coding and equalization techniques needed to tap the full capacity of the public network. The author examines the primary technical issues surrounding V.fast in relation to VLSI modem development. The discussion addresses implementation complexity and the impact of V.fast signal-correction algorithms on DSP requirements. A technology overview is provided for background.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ISDN terminal adaptors: a technology overview
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: Terminal adaptors (TAs) offer users a way to access the benefits of ISDN (high-speed throughput, error-free transmission, multiple line-sharing, local access to packet-switched networks, automatic number identification, and sophisticated diagnostics) without buying more expensive (and largely unavailable) ISDN-type terminals and computers. The TA can be viewed much like a modem, except that the modem connects terminals to the traditional analog network, whereas the terminal adaptor connects those analog-network terminals to the ISN network. Terminal adaptors will come to replace many modern installations, as users gradually convert from analog telephone lines to ISDN lines for their high-speed communications needs. The author discusses ISDN basics, TA fundamentals, rate adaption and features of available TAs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Standardization of provisions for ISDN/PSTN interworking of data terminals
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: The provision for the interworking of terminals on an Integrated Services Digital Network (ISDN) with terminals on existing networks is essential to the evolution of ISDN. The author considers the status of standards for the interworking of data terminals using circuit-mode services. The existing network of primary concern is the public switched telephone network (PSTN). The concepts discussed are equally applicable to scenarios where either or both the ISDN or existing network is private.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of an ISN terminal adaptor
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: Considers the following topics: hardware design of the ISDN terminal adaptor; verification of the operation of the telephone interfacing module; and initialisation of both the RS-232C interfacing module and the S interface module.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ISDN programmable communication interface (ISDN PCI)
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: Because of the varied requirements placed on the definition of the ISDN PCI it has emerged as a compromise that provides a powerful solution to application access to ISDN across many operating systems. The extendibility that has been factored into the design means that it provides a solution for the protocols required by applications today yet will allow access to other protocols to be added easily in the future.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementing the PATRICIA data structure for compression algorithms with finite size dictionaries
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: On the basis of the PATRICIA suffix tree, the author presents a simple way to implement a data structure for searching and updating the finite size dictionary in compression algorithms. For updating, each time a new entry is inserted into the tree, the internal node keeps the latest position rather than its old one. As in the normal PATRICIA tree, all the external nodes are put into a buffer, which shifts circularly. After the leaf nodes are exhausted, the oldest leaf node is deleted and put into the tree to represent new entries, and its old position is kept with a pointer. In this way, the updating procedure for all the internal nodes can be bypassed. Therefore, whenever the finite size dictionary is full, the spaces below the points of old positions can be replaced by new input data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The use of telecommunications to regenerate a rural area
publicationTitle: 1992 International Conference on Data Transmission - Advances in Modem and ISDN Technology and Applications
abstract: The author discusses the progress of a programme which aims to regenerate a rural economy through the introduction of advanced information technology. In the Highlands and Islands of Scotland the use of integrated approach to advanced telecommunications (ISDN, EDI, etc.) and IT is being promoted at a level appropriate to the individual companies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
